claims.text: Explanations, inconsistencies in explanations, and sources shape users' reliance on LLM responses.
The presence of explanations increases user reliance on correct LLM responses.
The presence of explanations increases user reliance on incorrect LLM responses.
Providing sources reduces user reliance on incorrect LLM responses.
Explanations exhibiting inconsistencies reduce user reliance on incorrect LLM responses.

evidence.description: Through a think-aloud study in which participants use an LLM-infused application to answer objective questions, we identify several features of LLM responses that shape users' reliance: explanations (supporting details for answers), inconsistencies in explanations, and sources.
We find that the presence of explanations increases reliance on both correct and incorrect responses.
We find that the presence of explanations increases reliance on both correct and incorrect responses.
However, we observe less reliance on incorrect responses when sources are provided...
However, we observe less reliance on incorrect responses [...] when explanations exhibit inconsistencies.

methodologies.name: Think-aloud study
methodologies.description: A qualitative study where participants use an LLM-infused application to answer objective questions to identify response features shaping reliance.

methodologies.name: Pre-registered controlled experiment
methodologies.description: A large-scale controlled experiment isolating the effects of explanations, sources, and inconsistencies on user reliance and accuracy.
